subject: Constraining two pathways to be equal (but resulting coefficients are unequal)

messages.author: 28f819885d30ea77
messages.subject: Constraining two pathways to be equal (but resulting coefficients are unequal)
parts:
Hi all

I am using SEM to build a higher-order model in Lavaan. I have 7 manifest variables, 3 of which load onto one latent variable (FAC1) and 4 of which load onto a second latent factor (FAC2). A higher-order third latent factor (FAC3) models the relation between FAC1 and FAC2, and I have constrained the pathway from FAC3 to the other two latent factors to be equal, by including this line of code:  FAC3 =~ b1*FAC1 + b1*FAC2

This constraint worked fine (i.e. the pathway from FAC3 to the other two factors was .77 for both) until I added in a manifest variable (FAC4) that directly predicts both FAC1 and FAC3, i.e. 
FAC1 ~ FAC4
FAC3 ~ FAC4 

When I include this additional pathway, the pathways from FAC3 to the latent factors FAC1 and FAC2 are no longer equal (now 57 and .73 respectively), despite the constraint I coded. Is the fact that I included a direct predictor pathway overriding the equal pathways constraint? Is there any way now to ensure the pathways to FAC1 and FAC2 from FAC3 are still equal, despite the addition of the manifest variable uniquely predicting FAC1 and FAC3 ? 

Help would be much appreciated working this out! If I have missed any crucial info from this, please let me know. Thanks in advance! 
Hannah

messages.subject: Re: Constraining two pathways to be equal (but resulting coefficients are unequal)
parts:
Hannah,

Can you post the model fit summary or a simple example that reproduces the same phenomenon?  The parameter labels (e.g., b1) should appear in parenthesis  between the name of the predictor and the raw estimate.  Are both parameters labeled as b1 in the summary of the second model?  Also, are you talking about the raw estimates?  It is entirely possible and not unusual for the standardized estimates to differ even when the raw estimates are constrained to equality.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Constraining two pathways to be equal (but resulting coefficients are unequal)
parts:
equal raw estimates but unequal standardized estimates - would you be able to elaborate on how this is possible? 

If that were not possible, there would be no reason to standardize.  A slope is standardized by transforming the slope into the value it would have if the predictor and outcome both had total variances of 1.  You can check whether you model implied variances are equal by checking the diagonal of this output (which are functions of estimated parameters, not necessarily the actual parameter estimates):

lavInspect(fit, "cov.all")

The standardized slopes would only be equal if you also constrained the residual variances of those variables to equality, along with the slopes (probably not an assumption you want to make, but certainly a testable constraint).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Cheers

parts: unless there is another reason to suspect model misidentification - this model and it's parameters are fine to report, yes?
If you model fits well and makes sense, and your tests are sensible, then yes, there is no problem with standardized coefficients differing when their unstandardized values are equal.
